title: Case Study: Faded Stucco Repaint in Missouri City, TX
description: A Missouri City, TX homeowner's faded, patchwork stucco exterior gets one unified charcoal repaint — see the walkthrough, warranty upgrade, and results.
author: Chris Petkau
imageAlt: Front entry exterior stucco repaint in Missouri City, TX, painted a unified charcoal by The Proud Paintbrush
content:
The fix for stucco that has faded into a mismatched patchwork of tan and greige isn't touch-up paint on the worst spots — it's a single, full-elevation repaint in one unified color. That's exactly what a Missouri City, TX homeowner named Jason chose after years of watching his stucco fade unevenly across the house, wall by wall, corner by corner.

Why Does Stucco Fade Unevenly in Missouri City, TX?

Stucco fades because Gulf Coast sun and humidity don't treat every wall the same. South- and west-facing elevations bake in full sun for most of the day and bleach out toward a warm tan. North-facing walls, shaded gables, and anything tucked behind a fence line or mature trees stay damp longer and drift toward a cooler, muddier greige. On a single-color stucco home, that uneven fade shows up fast — and it's especially common in Missouri City subdivisions where full-stucco construction is the norm rather than the exception. Jason's home was a textbook example: the sun-exposed elevations had faded tan, the shaded side yard and rear sections had gone greige, and the overall effect read as dated and patchy rather than intentional.

What Did Jason's Home Look Like Before the Repaint?

Walk the property before the repaint and the mismatch was obvious. The front entry and garage elevations, which get the most direct sun, had faded to a chalky tan. Turn the corner to the side and rear of the house and the stucco shifted to a flatter, cooler greige — same original color, years apart in appearance, purely from sun exposure. It wasn't a stucco failure or a structural issue; it was ordinary Gulf Coast weathering that had gone unaddressed for too long, and it was making a well-built home look older and less cared-for than it actually was.

Why Did Jason Choose The Proud Paintbrush?

Jason got more than one bid on the project, and The Proud Paintbrush wasn't the cheapest number on the table — it also wasn't the most expensive. What made the decision for him was confidence: after talking through the scope, the prep, and how we'd handle the stucco specifically, he said he felt sure we'd do the best job on his house, full stop. That's the conversation we want every homeowner to have before hiring anyone to touch their exterior — price matters, but it shouldn't be the only variable in the room.

What Happens During a Full Exterior Walkthrough?

Once the repaint was done, we walked the entire house with Jason, elevation by elevation — front entry, garage, side yard, side gable, backyard, rear patio, rear wing, and the two-story sections. The point of that walkthrough isn't a formality; it's where sloppy work gets caught, whether that's a missed cutline, a thin second coat, or caulk that didn't get touched. Jason went through the whole exterior with us and said he couldn't find anything wrong with the work. That's the standard we hold ourselves to on every job, not just the ones we expect to go well.

Why Did He Upgrade to the 5-Year Warranty?

Midway through the project, Jason took our recommendation and upgraded from our standard coverage to the full 2 & 5-Year Written Warranty. It costs a bit more upfront, but it buys a lot more peace of mind — especially on a stucco exterior in a climate that tests a paint job every summer. He didn't need convincing twice once he understood what the upgrade actually covered; it was an easy yes after seeing the quality of the work firsthand.

What Does the Finished Home Look Like Now?

Every elevation of Jason's home — front entry, garage, double garage, side yard, side gable, backyard, rear patio, rear wing, and the two-story sections — is now the same unified charcoal, top to bottom. No more chalky tan on one side and greige on the other, no more patchwork. The color reads as a single, deliberate choice, the kind of modern, cohesive exterior that Gulf Coast sun won't fade unevenly for years to come. It's the same transformation we bring to exterior painting projects across Missouri City, whether the issue is faded stucco, chalking brick, or a home that just hasn't been repainted since it was built.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does a full exterior stucco repaint take?

Timelines vary with square footage and the number of elevations, but a full stucco exterior typically includes pressure washing, caulking, stucco crack repair, priming any repaired or bare areas, and two full coats of finish paint. We'll give you a project-specific timeline during your in-home estimate.

Do you repair stucco cracks before painting?

Yes. Hairline stucco cracks are common on Gulf Coast homes as the substrate moves with temperature swings, and painting over them without repair just traps moisture underneath the new coat. We patch and seal cracks as part of the prep, not as an upcharge surprise.

What warranty comes with an exterior repaint?

Every exterior project comes with our standard workmanship warranty, and homeowners can upgrade to our 2 & 5-Year Written Warranty for extended coverage — the same upgrade Jason chose for his Missouri City home.

Cost depends on square footage, the number of elevations, and how much stucco repair is needed before painting. The most accurate way to get a number is a free in-home estimate, where we walk the exterior with you the way we did with Jason.
